requirements.title: Intake: three ways to create a work item
requirements.rationale: Work reaches nightshift as a text, an issue or a finished spec package, and each has to become the same thing before one process can drive it.

criteria.condition: an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items` with `{"workspace", "text", "kind"?, "no_plan_approval"?}`, the workspace is registered, the text has 1 to 20,000 Unicode code points and `kind` is absent, `defect` or `change_request`
criteria.action: store a work item with the next number (one above the highest number ever given over all workspaces, starting at 1), the kind (`change_request` when absent), the title (the first line of the text, cut to 80 code points), the source `{type: "text"}` with the text, the state `new` and `plan_approval` (false when `no_plan_approval` is true, else true); create the item's thread with a first entry of kind `created`; append the event `item.created`; and call every creation hook registered with `OnCreated`
criteria.contract: status 201 with the item as {number, workspace, kind, title, state, state_since, created_at, plan_approval, source {type, …}, parent, children, thread, waiting_on, markers}, `thread` being `/api/v1/threads/<id>`; items created by concurrent requests get distinct numbers with no gap; the event's data is `{item, workspace, state, thread}`

setup: an inbox and an item service over a copy of the store template and the event log; the workspaces `demo` and `other` are known through the service's workspace source (the Get and List of package 02's workspace.Service), a stub in the tests of this package that need no removal
one creation hook registered that records its argument
check.pseudocode: new file internal/item/routes_test.go, through the router, a table over {text only -> kind change_request, plan_approval true; kind defect; no_plan_approval true -> plan_approval false; a text of 3 lines -> title is line 1; a first line of 200 code points -> title has 80; a text of exactly 20,000 code points -> 201}: r = post('/api/v1/items', body); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json fields; assert get('/api/v1/threads/' + id).json.entries[0].kind == 'created'; assert the event log's last event type == 'item.created'; assert the creation hook saw the item. Then 20 concurrent posts over two workspaces: assert the numbers are 1 more than before .. 20 more, each once

criteria.condition: a request to `POST /api/v1/items` has a body that is not a JSON object, names no workspace, carries a text that is empty or longer than 20,000 Unicode code points or a `kind` other than `defect` and `change_request`, or names a workspace that is not registered
criteria.action: refuse the request and store nothing
criteria.contract: status 400 with `error_type: invalid_request` and a message naming the member, or status 404 with `error_type: not_found` for the unregistered workspace; no item, no thread and no event is written, and the next item created gets the number it would have got

check.pseudocode: in internal/item/routes_test.go, a table over {'not json', {} , text '', text of 20,001 code points, a text of 20,000 two-byte characters -> 201 (counted in code points, not bytes), kind 'spec', kind 'bogus' -> 400 invalid_request; workspace 'nope' -> 404 not_found}: r = post('/api/v1/items', body); assert r.status and r.json.error_type; assert count(items) and count(threads) unchanged; then a valid post gets number previous+1

criteria.condition: an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/import` with `{"workspace", "issue": N, "no_plan_approval"?}` for a registered workspace, and the hub answers `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{N}` with an issue that is not a pull request and whose comments it could read
criteria.action: read the issue with the worker token, read the further comments from `GET …/issues/{N}/comments` with `cursor` set to each `next_cursor` until it is null or 1,000 comments are read, and store a work item in the state `new` whose kind is `defect` when the issue's labels hold `af:defect` or `bug`, compared ignoring case, and `change_request` otherwise, whose title is the issue's title and whose source is `{type: "issue", issue, url, title, body, labels, comments: [{author, body, created_at}], comments_truncated}`; then create the thread, append the event and call the creation hooks as for a text
criteria.contract: status 201 with the item; `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` answers the source with every comment read, oldest first; `comments_truncated` is true only when the hub had more than 1,000 comments; the hub saw requests bearing the worker token only

setup: internal/hubtest extended with scriptable issues: an issue thread per workspace and number, its comments paged 100 a page, a `comments_error`, `is_pr` and a forge error to answer with
the item service's hub client pointed at the fake hub
check.pseudocode: new file internal/item/import_test.go, through the router, a table over the fake hub's issue 7 {labels ['bug'] -> defect; ['af:defect'] -> defect; ['Bug','ui'] -> defect; ['ui'] -> change_request; [] -> change_request; 250 comments over 3 pages -> source.comments has 250 in order; 1,100 comments -> 1,000 and comments_truncated true; no_plan_approval true -> plan_approval false}: r = post('/api/v1/items/import', {workspace: 'demo', issue: 7}); assert r.status == 201; assert kind, title, source; assert every hub request bore the worker token

criteria.condition: an issue import names an issue that an item of the workspace was already created from, or the hub is not available to the worker token, or the hub answers the issue or a page of its comments with an error, or the issue's answer carries a `comments_error`, or the issue has `is_pr: true`
criteria.action: refuse the import and store nothing, checking for the existing item before any request to the hub
criteria.contract: status 409 `conflict` with the message `issue #<N> is already item <M>` (also when item M is `abandoned`), sending no hub request; status 503 `hub_unavailable` while `Available(worker)` is false; status 502 `hub_error` with the message `<hub error_type>: <hub message>` for a hub error and for a `comments_error`; status 409 `conflict` with `#<N> is a pull request`; status 400 `invalid_request` for an `issue` that is not a positive integer or a body carrying both `issue` and `spec` or neither; status 404 `not_found` for a workspace that is not registered; in every case no item, thread or event is written

criteria.condition: an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/import` with `{"workspace", "spec": "NN"}` for a registered workspace, and the package with that number in `.specs/` at the tip of the workspace's default branch loads, validates with no error, has the status `active` and has at least one open task
criteria.action: read the workspace's `head_sha` from the hub, bring a clone of the workspace to that commit with `gitclone.Sync` of package 02, find the package directory with `afspec.DiscoverSpecs`, load it with `afspec.LoadSpec`, validate it with `afspec.ValidateInRoot` and read its open tasks with `OpenTasks`, and store a work item in the state `new` with the kind `spec`, the package's title, `plan_approval` true and the source `{type: "spec", spec_id, spec_name, dir}`; then create the thread, append the event and call the creation hooks as for a text
criteria.contract: status 201 with the item; `source.dir` is the package's directory relative to the repository root (`.specs/04_greeting`); the item's state is `new`

requirements.title: Item states, queries, abandoning and linked items
requirements.rationale: Seven later packages move items; one function that knows every allowed move keeps an item from reaching a state by a road the person was never shown.

criteria.condition: a part of nightshift calls the item service's `Transition(ctx, number, to, reason)` with a state the transition table allows from the item's current state (new -> planning, ready, abandoned; planning -> awaiting_approval, ready, abandoned; awaiting_approval -> planning, ready, abandoned; ready -> implementing, abandoned; implementing -> reviewing, abandoned; reviewing -> implementing, landing, abandoned; landing -> implementing, verifying, abandoned; verifying -> publishing, awaiting_approval; publishing -> done; done and abandoned -> none)
criteria.action: set the item's state and `state_since`, append to the item's thread an entry of kind `state` with the text `<from> -> <to>`, followed by `: <reason>` when a reason is given, marking the thread unread when the new state is `done` or `abandoned`, append the event `item.updated` with the data `{item, workspace, state, thread}`, and then call every hook registered with `OnChange` with the item before and after
criteria.contract: the call returns the item in its new state; the state, the entry and the event are written in one store transaction; a hook's error is written to the daemon's log and undoes nothing

setup: an item service over a copy of the store template with an injected clock
a test helper that puts an item into any state by walking allowed transitions
check.pseudocode: new file internal/item/item_test.go, a table with one row per allowed pair of the transition table (22 rows), each on an item put into the from state: it = svc.Transition(ctx, n, to, 'because'); assert it.State == to; assert the thread's last entry == {kind: 'state', text: from + ' -> ' + to + ': because'}; assert thread.unread == (to in {done, abandoned}); assert the event log's last event == item.updated with state to; assert the OnChange hook saw (from, to). One row with an empty reason asserts the text has no colon suffix; one hook returning an error leaves the state at to

criteria.condition: `Transition` is called for a number no item has, with a name that is not one of the eleven states, with the state the item is in, or with a state the transition table does not allow from the item's current state
criteria.action: refuse the transition and leave the item as it is
criteria.contract: the call returns `item.ErrNotFound` for the unknown number and otherwise an error that is `item.ErrTransition` and whose text is `item <N>: <from> -> <to> is not allowed`; no state, entry or event is written and no hook is called; of two concurrent calls for the same allowed move exactly one succeeds and the other gets `ErrTransition`

check.pseudocode: in internal/item/item_test.go, a table over every ordered pair of the eleven states that the transition table does not hold (99 rows, the 11 same-state pairs among them) plus {unknown number -> ErrNotFound, to 'bogus' -> ErrTransition}: err = svc.Transition(ctx, n, to, ''); assert errors.Is(err, want); assert state, entry count and event count unchanged. Then 8 goroutines call Transition(n, 'planning') on one new item: assert exactly 1 nil error and 7 ErrTransition, and one `state` entry

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/items`, optionally with `workspace=<slug>` and `state=<state>`
criteria.action: answer every item, or those of the workspace and in the state named, in ascending order of number, each with `waiting_on` as `{id, kind, question}` of the item's oldest open decision or null, and `markers` as the names of the registered marker functions (`RegisterMarker(name, fn)`) that report true for the item, in registration order
criteria.contract: status 200 with `{"items": [<item>, …]}`; an item is {number, workspace, kind, title, state, state_since, created_at, plan_approval, source {type, …}, parent, children, thread, waiting_on, markers} with `source` reduced to `{type}` and, by type, `issue` and `url`, or `spec_id` and `spec_name`, or `item`; no item matching is `{"items": []}`

criteria.action: answer the item as the list does, with the whole of its source (the `text`; or the issue's `issue`, `url`, `title`, `body`, `labels`, `comments` and `comments_truncated`; or the package's `spec_id`, `spec_name` and `dir`; or the `item` it was created from and the `text`), its `parent` and its `children` in ascending order
criteria.contract: status 200 with the item; `waiting_on` and `markers` as in the list

criteria.condition: a request to `GET /api/v1/items`, `GET /api/v1/items/{number}` or `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/abandon` names a number no item has, a number that is not a positive decimal integer, a `state` that is not one of the eleven states, or a `workspace` that is not registered
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: status 404 `not_found` for the unknown number and the unregistered workspace; status 400 `invalid_request` for the malformed number and the unknown state; the body is `{"error_type", "message"}`

criteria.condition: an authenticated client sends `POST /api/v1/items/{number}/abandon`, or a part of nightshift calls the item service's `Abandon(ctx, number, reason)`, for an item in the state `new`, `planning`, `awaiting_approval`, `ready`, `implementing`, `reviewing` or `landing`
criteria.action: call every hook registered with `OnAbandon(name, fn)` with the item, in registration order, writing a hook's error to the item's thread as an entry of kind `abandon_hook_failed` with the text `<name>: <error>` and going on; close every open decision of the item with the reason `item abandoned`; and move the item to `abandoned` through the transition function
criteria.contract: status 200 with the item, its state `abandoned` and `waiting_on` null (the function returns the same item); the item's thread is unread; every hook was called once, before the state changed; the item's former open decisions have the state `closed`

criteria.contract: status 409 with `error_type: conflict` and the message `item <N> is <state> and cannot be abandoned`, or `item <N> is already abandoned`; `Abandon` returns an error that is `item.ErrTransition`; no entry and no event is written

criteria.condition: a part of nightshift calls the item service's `CreateLinked(ctx, parent, kind, text)` with the number of an existing item, the kind `defect` or `change_request` and a text of 1 to 20,000 Unicode code points
criteria.action: store a new work item in the parent's workspace with the next number, the kind, the title (the first line of the text, cut to 80 code points), the source `{type: "item", item: <parent>}` with the text, the state `new`, `plan_approval` true and `parent` set to the parent's number; create its thread; append to the parent's thread an entry of kind `linked_item` with the text `item <N> created: <title>`, not marking it unread; append the event `item.created`; and call the creation hooks
criteria.contract: the call returns the new item; the parent's `children` holds its number; an unknown parent returns `item.ErrNotFound`, and a kind `spec` or a text outside the bounds an error that is `item.ErrInvalid`, each creating nothing

requirements.title: Threads, unread, and a workspace's removal
requirements.rationale: The person reads what happened in one place per item, and should be shown only what is new since they last looked.

criteria.action: for any work item, keep exactly one thread of kind `item`, created in the transaction that creates the item; for any registered workspace, return from the inbox's `WorkspaceThread(ctx, slug)` the one thread of kind `workspace` of that slug, and from `BriefThread(ctx)` the one thread of kind `brief` of the installation, each created at the first call and the same thread at every later one
criteria.contract: a thread has an id (a positive integer, never given twice), a kind, the workspace and the item where it has them, and a title: the item's title, `workspace <slug>` or `daily brief`; concurrent first calls of `WorkspaceThread` for one slug return the same id

criteria.condition: a part of nightshift calls the inbox's `Append(ctx, threadID, Entry{Kind, Text, Unread})` for an existing thread, with a kind matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` and a text that is not empty
criteria.action: store the entry with the next `seq` of that thread (starting at 1) and the time of the injected clock, set the thread's `last_activity` to that time, mark the thread unread when `Unread` is true and it is not unread already, remembering that entry as the first unread one, and append the event `thread.updated` with the data `{thread, unread}`
criteria.contract: the call returns the entry with its `seq` and `time`; the entries of a thread read back in `seq` order; an entry with `Unread` false leaves a read thread read; an unknown thread returns `inbox.ErrNotFound` and a malformed kind or an empty text an error that is `inbox.ErrInvalid`, each writing nothing

criteria.contract: status 200 with `{"items": [<thread>, …], "next_cursor": <string or null>}`; a thread is `{id, path, kind, workspace, item, title, unread, last_activity, open_decisions: [{id, kind, question}]}` with `path` `/api/v1/threads/<id>`; following `next_cursor` until it is null yields every matching thread once; a workspace filter leaves out the brief thread

requirements.title: Decisions: a registry of kinds, answers and their handlers
requirements.rationale: Eleven kinds of question from seven packages reach the person through one machinery, so that every one of them waits, is answered and takes effect in the same way.

criteria.condition: a part of nightshift calls the inbox's `Open(ctx, OpenRequest{Kind, Thread, Question, Evidence, Recommended, Blocks})` with a kind declared through `RegisterKind(Kind{Name, Options: [{Key, Does, CommentRequired}]})`, an existing thread, a question that is not empty and a `Recommended` that is the key of one of the kind's options
criteria.action: store a decision in the state `open` with the next id (starting at 1), the thread and its workspace and item, the question, the evidence, what it blocks and a copy of the kind's options as they are at that moment, the options added through `AddOption(kind, Option)` among them and the recommended one marked; append to the thread an entry of kind `decision_opened` with the text `<kind>: <question>`, marking it unread; and append the event `decision.opened` with the data `{decision, kind, thread, workspace, item}`
criteria.contract: the call returns the decision as {id, kind, state, thread, workspace, item, question, evidence: [{label, url or text}], options: [{key, does, comment_required, recommended}], blocks, opened_at, answer, closed_reason} with `answer` and `closed_reason` null; exactly one option has `recommended: true`; an option added to the kind after the decision was opened does not appear in it; the thread is in the views `unread` and `action`

requirements.title: Waiting, reminding and telling the person
requirements.rationale: A decision that waits in silence waits for days; the person has to learn that they are needed without watching the inbox, and nothing may be lost while they are away.

criteria.action: take no option for it, however long it is open, and append to its thread an entry of kind `decision_reminder` with the text `<kind>: open since <opened_at>: <question>`, marking the thread unread, each time 24 hours have passed since the later of its opening and its last reminder, one entry also when several such periods have passed at once
criteria.contract: a decision open for 23 hours 59 minutes has no reminder; one open for 24 hours has one; after 48 hours it has two; a daemon whose clock moved 7 days between two passes writes one reminder at that pass and the next one 24 hours later; the decision is still `open` with `answer` null; an answered or closed decision gets none
